welcome_page.description:

Taking part is voluntary and you can skip any question. Your answers are not linked to your name, and no public authority receives them.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

questionnaire.title: Public transport – Safety and comfort

questions.text: What problems do you meet at stops or when getting on and off?

options.text: Hard to get on or off the vehicle
Broken or poorly kept stops (e.g. broken lifts, damaged shelters)
Stop or vehicle cannot be used with a wheelchair, walker or stroller
Vehicles too crowded to get on with a stroller or wheelchair
The ramp does not work or is not deployed when needed
Vehicles so full that I have to wait for the next one
No sidewalk or walkway to reach the stop
No real-time arrival information, on screen or announced

questions.text: When you cross the road to reach or leave a stop, how safe do you feel?
questions.help: Think of traffic lights, zebra crossings, footbridges or underpasses near the stops you use.

options.text: I avoid some stops because crossing to them feels unsafe
I often feel unsafe when I cross
I sometimes go a longer way to cross more safely
I feel safe, but I have to be careful
I feel safe: the crossings are well protected

questions.text: When you use public transport, which of these situations make you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Unsafe behaviour from drivers, riders or pedestrians
Lack of safe or adequate stops, crossings or lighting

questions.text: During the day, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you use public transport? (Harassment includes unwanted comments, following, touching, or intimidating behaviour directed at you.)
In the evening or after dark, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you use public transport?
When you feel unsafe in the evening, what do you change?
questions.help: You can choose more than one answer.

options.text: I share my location with someone
I ask someone to come with me
I use a different means of transport

questions.text: When you use public transport, what makes you feel less secure from crime or harassment? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Long waits at stops in the evening
Places with few people around (isolated or deserted areas)
People behaving aggressively or in an intimidating way
Poor maintenance (e.g. abandoned buildings, graffiti, broken infrastructure)
No surveillance or security measures (e.g. no cameras, no staff)
Incidents that happened to me or were reported in the area
Few cues to find my way without sight (e.g. no tactile paths or audio announcements)
No visual information about stops or service changes

questions.text: After dark, does poor lighting at stops or on the way to them make you change your route or the time you travel?
When you use public transport, have you experienced or do you fear harassment because of who you are or how you look (e.g. gender, appearance, origin, age)?
How comfortable do you feel when the vehicle or stop is crowded?
How well do the timetable and frequency on your routes fit your needs?

options.text: Not at all: it's too rare or unreliable
Only for some regular trips (e.g. work or school)
For planned trips, but not at short notice
Well, but I plan around the timetable
Very well: it's so frequent I don't need to plan

questions.text: How stressful are unexpected delays or cancellations for you?
When the service is late or unreliable, what do you do?

options.text: I leave earlier, just in case
I change route or travel time
I don't rely on it for important trips
I use another way of travelling instead
I have no alternative: I wait, sometimes for a long time
I arrive late for work, school or appointments
It doesn't change what I do

questions.text: On hot days, are waits at stops without shade hard for you?
Do you need a seat at the stop or on board, and often find none?
Do unclear or missing signs at stops and stations make it hard to find your way?
